title: Onramp velocity checkpoint and escalations brief
body:
Meeting: Solutions Eng + ProServices weekly sync (Onramp velocity focus)
Date: 2028-06-01
Time: 10:00-11:00 PT
Attendees: Aisha Raman (owner), Ben Carter, Maya Singh, Diego Alvarez, Priya Nair, Luis Moreno (SRE), Sasha Kent (Customer Success - Veridian)
Objective: Rapid status check on active onboarding customers, escalate unresolved technical blockers, align capacity and rollout windows for Dedicated/Demo clusters.

Agenda:
- Quick round of per-customer status (5m each)
- Top blockers and who owns escalation path
- Capacity and scheduling conflicts for Dedicated runs
- Test harness and perf validation status
- Action items and commitments

Summary notes (per-customer):
1) Veridian Health (priority: high)
   - Status: In validation. Ingest pipeline tested; model routing to dedicated pool partially validated.
   - Blocker: VPC peering intermittently drops during load tests; observed 502s when KV cache warms up for long contexts.
   - Root cause hypothesis: MTU mismatch + egress policy causing TCP resets. Luis to validate network path and MTU with cloud infra team.
   - Workaround: Reduce batch size and enable conservative batching for peak windows; re-run validation with smaller concurrency.
   - Notes: Customer requested canary on dedicated capacity on 2028-06-08 morning PST. Need SRE on-call to approve peering maintenance window.

2) Tidewater Analytics (priority: medium)
   - Status: Model quantization experiments complete; quality regression flagged on specific prompts (finance templates).
   - Blocker: Slight BLEU-style drop for structured table outputs after int8 quantization.
   - Action: Maya to run targeted eval set and open regression ticket with Research (JIRA:PROJ-4321). Suggested mitigation: use 8-bit with activation-scaling profile B instead of profile A.
   - Rollout plan: canary 5% traffic next Tuesday, hold if more than 2% failure in structured parsing tests.

3) MaraCommerce (priority: low)
   - Status: SDK integration done; client reported slow initial token latency on cold-start.
   - Investigation: likely insufficient KV cache warmup for typical prompt prefixes. Diego to add prefix caching in the SDK wrapper and propose TTL for cache entries.
   - Customer request: improved observability on per-call token latency. Product to provide a dashboard snippet for their team.

4) BlueCove (priority: medium-high)
   - Status: Dedicated pool requested; procurement and billing cleared. Infra scheduling conflict: both BlueCove and Veridian requested same GPU rack on 2028-06-08.
   - Resolution path: Aisha to propose time-sliced allocation (Veridian morning, BlueCove afternoon) and coordinate live failover policy. If BlueCove needs full-day slot, escalate to Capacity Planning (Slack pinged).

Top cross-customer blockers and notes:
- Network/VPC peering flakiness (Veridian) — SRE follow-up required, possible maintenance window. Owner: Luis Moreno. ETA: 2028-06-03 to confirm root cause and propose fix.
- Quantization regressions on some structured outputs (Tidewater) — Research + SE looking into profile tuning. Owner: Maya Singh. ETA: 2028-06-05 for targeted eval results.
- Scheduling conflict on Dedicated rack (Veridian vs BlueCove) — Capacity team involvement needed. Owner: Aisha Raman. ETA: 2028-06-02 propose temporary allocation.
- Observability gaps for customer-side latency traces — Product to surface per-customer view. Owner: Priya Nair. ETA: 2028-06-09 include dashboard snippet and sample API call trace.

Test / validation updates:
- Perf harness: new load generator added to reproduce KV-warmup spikes (script: gh:infra/perf/loadgen/warmup_v2). Diego ran a 30-minute soak and reproduced 502s at 550 rps for long sequences (>2048 tokens).
- Canary instrumentation: added token-level timing logs and sampling (10%) to avoid excessive telemetry cost. Confirmed works in staging.

Action items (owner, due):
- Luis Moreno: Complete VPC path and MTU validation for Veridian, propose maintenance window. Due 2028-06-03. Linked: JIRA:INT-9876.
- Maya Singh: Run targeted evaluation on Tidewater prompt set, document quantization profile tradeoffs, open Research triage ticket. Due 2028-06-05. Linked: JIRA:PROJ-4321.
- Diego Alvarez: Implement prefix caching change in SDK wrapper for MaraCommerce and test cold-start latency improvement. Due 2028-06-07.
- Aisha Raman: Coordinate Dedicated rack schedule and propose time-sliced allocation; escalate if BlueCove requires full-day. Due 2028-06-02.
- Priya Nair: Draft and share per-customer latency dashboard snippet and sample tracing artifact. Due 2028-06-09.
- Ben Carter: Prepare rollback playbook for canary quantization changes (Tidewater) and validate automatic fallback to float32 variant. Due 2028-06-04.

Risks and mitigation suggestions:
- If VPC peering fix requires >2 hours downtime, recommend moving Veridian canary to a later date to avoid missed SLA windows. Notify customer-facing PM.
- Quantization rollback: ensure float32 variant is tagged and available with same routing policy to avoid cold-start overhead on fallback.
- Capacity contention: publish transparent allocation calendar for dedicated racks to reduce ad-hoc conflicts.

Open questions for leadership / follow-up:
- Can Capacity Planning reserve a short-term overflow pool for high-priority canaries? (Aisha will escalate.)
- What's the approved SLO for peering-maintenance downtime for enterprise customers? (Product/legal input needed.)

Notes to self / friction points observed during sync:
- Customer success frequently asks for per-call traces; our current telemetry sampling rate is conservative and missing some tail events. Consider increasing sampling for active canaries.
- Onboarding playbook needs a short checklist for network prechecks (MTU, firewall rules, DNS) — add to Confluence runbook.

Next sync focus (2028-06-08):
- Confirm Veridian peering fix or maintenance window outcome.
- Tidewater targeted eval results and canary readiness.
- Finalize dedicated rack schedule and notify customers.

Document versioning / links:
- Perf harness repo: github.com/redwood/infra/tree/main/perf/loadgen
- Triage tickets referenced: JIRA:PROJ-4321, JIRA:INT-9876

End of brief.
